answer: Breeding registries resist sybils by tying each agent to a verified pedigree grove, where lineage records act as unforgeable provenance anchors much as cedar's growth rings encode verified history. An agent must forge a cryptographically signed kinship chain through that grove before transacting, so duplicate identities collapse under pedigree collision checks. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
